record.paper_title: Frequently hypercyclic operators: recent advances and open problems
record.original_question: If T is a frequently hypercyclic operator, must the direct sum operator T⊕T also be frequently hypercyclic?

evidence.quote:
Problem 10. If T is a frequently hypercyclic operator, is then also T ⊕ T frequently
hypercyclic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a separable infinite-dimensional Banach (or Fréchet) space, and let $T:X\to X$ be a continuous linear operator. A vector $x\in X$ is called frequently hypercyclic for $T$ if for every nonempty open set $U\subseteq X$ the set
$$N(x,U)=\{n\in\mathbb{N}: T^n x\in U\}$$
has positive lower density, i.e.
$$\underline{\mathrm{dens}}\,N(x,U)=\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{\#(N(x,U)\cap[1,N])}{N}>0.$$
The operator $T$ is called frequently hypercyclic if it admits a frequently hypercyclic vector. The direct sum $T\oplus T$ is the operator on $X\oplus X$ defined by $(T\oplus T)(x,y)=(Tx,Ty)$.

Question: If $T$ is a frequently hypercyclic operator on $X$, must $T\oplus T$ also be frequently hypercyclic on $X\oplus X$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question was answered in the negative by Q. Menet in "Linear chaos and frequent hypercyclicity" (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2017), where a frequently hypercyclic operator $T$ is constructed such that $T\oplus T$ is not frequently hypercyclic. Subsequent work (Bayart–Grivaux–Matheron–Menet on hereditarily frequently hypercyclic operators) provides further counterexamples among weighted shifts.

status_evidence.title: Linear chaos and frequent hypercyclicity (arXiv:1410.7173)
status_evidence.snippet: Menet's 2017 TAMS paper constructing a frequently hypercyclic operator T such that T⊕T fails to be frequently hypercyclic.
status_evidence.claim: Menet (2017) gave a negative answer: there exists a frequently hypercyclic T with T⊕T not frequently hypercyclic.

status_evidence.title: Hereditarily frequently hypercyclic operators and disjoint frequent hypercyclicity (arXiv:2409.07103)
status_evidence.snippet: Exhibits two frequently hypercyclic weighted shifts whose direct sum is not frequently hypercyclic.
status_evidence.claim: Further counterexamples confirm that frequent hypercyclicity is not preserved under direct sums with itself in general.
